# Production Mistakes Deep Dive

## Overview

Recurring themes from production Go engineering discussions (including widely shared checklists on X): timeouts, leaks, default clients, lock+I/O, and observability gaps. This chapter maps each mistake to **runtime symptoms** and **fixes** covered elsewhere in this part.


## Diagram: Incident loop

```text
flow:
  [Prof]
       |
       v
  [Trace]

  [Trace]
       |
       v
  [Fix]
```

## The List (Mapped)

| Mistake | Symptom | Deep dive / fix |
|---------|---------|-----------------|
| No context timeouts | Goroutine + FD growth | [Context trees](226-context-cancel-tree.qmd), [netpoller](213-netpoller-network-io.qmd) |
| Unbounded goroutines | RSS↑, sched latency | [Scheduler](201-scheduler-gmp-deep-dive.qmd), [leaks](220-goroutine-leaks-diagnosis.qmd) |
| Default `http.Client` | Hung dials/TLS | [Transport pool](225-http-transport-conn-pool.qmd) |
| Errors as strings | Untestable retries | [Error cost](236-error-interface-cost.qmd) |
| nil vs empty JSON | Client contract breaks | [encoding stdlib](../98-stdlib/985-encoding-json-csv-xml.qmd) |
| Unbounded channels | Memory spikes | [Channel internals](203-channels-select-internals.qmd) |
| Lock held over I/O | Throughput collapse | [Mutex runtime](227-mutex-semaphore-runtime.qmd) |
| `time.After` in hot select | Timer/alloc churn | [Timers](214-timers-time-after-pitfalls.qmd) |
| DB without limits/context | Connection storms | [HTTP/DB practices](../08-web/64-db-postgres-redis.qmd) |
| Logs without IDs/metrics | Blind incidents | [slog](../98-stdlib/981-fmt-log-slog.qmd), observability parts |

## Incident Playbook

```text
1. NumGoroutine / FD count / RSS chart
2. goroutine pprof (wait sites)
3. mutex/block profile if CPU low
4. trace 200–500ms around incident
5. check client/server timeouts
6. check deploy diff for "go func" and "time.After"
```

## Engineering Questions (From "knowing Go")

1. Do you need concurrency at all?
2. Goroutine or worker pool?
3. Channel or mutex?
4. How does context propagate?
5. Did you run `-race`, pprof, `-gcflags=-m`?

## Mini Lab

Take any service and grep:

```bash
rg -n 'http\\.Get|http\\.DefaultClient|time\\.After|go func|context\\.Background\\(\\)' --glob '*.go'
```

Classify each hit as safe or debt.
